title: Live Broadcast Comments and Reactions
summary: Fan out live comments and burst reactions to millions of concurrent viewers of a single stream.
statement:
Design the real-time interactive overlay for a live video platform where viewers post comments and tap emoji reactions while watching a live broadcast.

Functional requirements:
- Viewers watching a live broadcast see new comments and floating emoji reactions within about a second.
- Viewers joining mid-broadcast receive the most recent comments and can scroll earlier chat history.
- Creators and moderators can mute abusive users or delete comments in real time.
- When a celebrity stream receives thousands of comments and tens of thousands of reactions per second, clients must remain smooth rather than freezing.

Scale to assume:
- 50 million concurrent viewers across all active broadcasts.
- A single marquee broadcast can draw 5 million concurrent viewers.
- Peak interaction rate on one broadcast: 20,000 comments per second and 200,000 reactions per second.
hints: Sending 200,000 individual reaction events per second to each of 5 million viewers means `10^12` messages per second—impossible and unreadable on screen. How should comments and reactions be shaped differently?
A single server can hold perhaps 50,000 to 100,000 open connections, so one marquee broadcast spans dozens or hundreds of edge servers. Draw the fan-out tree from one incoming comment to all of them.
How do you keep one viral 5-million-viewer broadcast from starving thousands of smaller 100-viewer streams?
expectations: Clarifies acceptable latency (~1s), ordering (causal/approximate rather than strict total order), persistence needs (comments saved, individual reaction taps ephemeral), and client display rate limits.
Calculates why naive per-event fan-out (`5M * 220K/s`) fails both network bandwidth and client UI rendering.

Handles comments and reactions with distinct pipelines: persists comments and samples/rate-limits display on mega-streams, while aggregating reactions in memory into short windows (for example per-second counts per emoji) before broadcasting.

Builds a hierarchical pub/sub fan-out tree (root broadcast topic -> regional relays -> WebSocket/SSE edge connection gateways) so each edge gateway receives a stream's payload once and fans it out locally in memory.
Serves join catch-up and backward scrolling from a time-ordered comment store (`(broadcast_id, comment_id)`) cached at the CDN/edge so millions of simultaneous joins do not hit storage.
Propagates moderation deletes and user mutes over the same broadcast channel as control events while enforcing mute lists at the write API.
Isolates viral broadcasts onto dedicated shards/topics and sheds load gracefully (dropping reaction granularity or sampling comments) under extreme spikes.
